text:
A: Hiya, you alright? I'm Daniel.
B: Yes. Hi. Jurgita.
A: Jurgita, nice to meet you. Last one for me. Where are you calling from?
B: Wakefield.
A: Oh, Wakefield, I'm up the A1 that way sometimes for work. I'm Peterborough. How's your day been?
B: Tired. Three long days in care home this week. Twelve hours.
A: Oof. You must be knackered. Is it a residential home?
B: Yes. Old people, lot of dementia. I am senior care assistant. Medication, care plans, and also washing, dressing, everything.
A: That's proper work, that. My mum worked in a GP surgery, she always said the care home staff were the ones holding it all together. What's the best bit and the worst bit?
B: Best bit, residents, some of them. Worst bit, management. They change rota every week without asking nobody. You look at board and you are working Sunday.
A: Ah. Right. I should confess, I do the rotas at my place. I'm operations manager at a distribution centre, about a hundred and forty staff.
B: So you are the one.
A: Ha, I'm the one, yeah. But in my defence, I try really hard not to do that. Two weeks' notice minimum unless the building's on fire. Because I know if I mess about with someone's shifts, they've got kids to pick up, childcare, whatever. You lose people's goodwill like that, and you don't get it back.
B: Two weeks. Our manager does two days.
A: That's not on. Honestly. Do you get a say at all, like a request book or anything?
B: There is a book. Nobody reads it.
A: Classic. What's your husband do, is he in care as well?
B: No, he drives forklift. Warehouse, off M62. Nights, because it pays more.
A: Ah, so he's one of mine, sort of. Not literally. Good forklift drivers are worth their weight in gold, tell him that from me. Do you two ever see each other?
B: Sunday. Sometimes.
A: That's tough. My wife's a teacher, and I moan about our holidays not matching, but that's nothing compared to days and nights.
B: Is okay. We are used to it. And money is better.
A: Have you ever thought about going for team leader or deputy? You sound like you know exactly how it should be run.
B: They asked me. Team leader. But is more paperwork, more meetings, and little bit more money. Not worth it.
A: Yeah, that's fair. Though honestly, the best supervisors I've got are the ones who were annoyed about how it was being done. They're the ones who fix it. And you'd be the one writing the rota.
B: Hm. Then nobody changes it without asking.
A: Exactly. Two weeks' notice, Jurgita's rules.
B: Maybe. I think about it. If money is good.
A: Ask what the money is, that's the first thing. Never say no before you've seen the number.
B: Yes. This is true. I got Michael Kors bag in sale, forty pound, because I look at number first.
A: Forty quid? That's a bargain, my wife would be—
